newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to reshuffle cabinet in September - report.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to reshuffle cabinet in September - report.

text.p: Taiwan will postpone a cabinet reshuffle until September to maintain stability within the ruling Nationalist Party ahead of a key party congress, the United Evening News reported on Sunday.

The newspaper quoted high-ranking officials as saying Vice President and Premier Lien Chan would keep his promise and offer to step down as premier in late July or early August, but President Lee Teng-hui would not approve his resignation until September.
The delay would allow the Nationalist Party to proceed with its 15th party congress without any distraction, the report said.
The ruling party is expected to re-elect a party chairman and vice chairmen and discuss major party affairs during the August 23-27 meeting.
Lien, under fire for a perceived breakdown of law and order, has said he plans to step down as premier after key constitutional reforms are carried out in July.
The ruling party announced a modest cabinet shake-up in May in a bid to ease public anger.
